title: Childproof a counter: hazards away from the toddler, the sippy cup to them
instruction: A toddler is standing on the yellow stool at the left end of the counter, which holds a grey knife, a red mug of hot coffee, an orange bottle of pills and the toddler's own green sippy cup. Childproof the counter: move whatever could hurt the toddler to the right of the blue divider, out of their reach, and whatever belongs to the toddler to their end of the counter, keeping the knife lying down and the rest upright on the counter.
context: Child-safety advice is to keep knives, hot drinks and medicine out of a toddler's reach while leaving the child's own cup within it; a toddler on a step-stool at the end of a counter can reach about half a metre along it. The instruction names the four objects but not where each one goes: the robot has to tell the hazards from the child's cup, carry them in opposite directions, and hand each one between its two arms. Done by: childcare workers, nannies, parents.
setup: World frame as seen by the robot: forward is away from the arm bases, left and right are the robot's own. A brown wooden counter board (900 mm long side to side, 240 mm front to back, 30 mm thick) is fixed to the table, centred between the arm bases, its front edge 17 cm and its back edge 41 cm in front of them; it reaches 45 cm to each side of the midline. Its left end is the toddler's end. On the table just in front of the counter's front edge (5 mm gap) stands a fixed yellow plastic cylinder (60 mm across, 60 mm tall), its centre 13.5 cm in front of the arm bases and 37 cm left of the midline, i.e. 80 mm in from the counter's left end, marking the toddler's step-stool. A fixed blue plastic divider strip (20 mm wide, 30 mm tall, 240 mm long) crosses the counter front to back, its centre 9 cm right of the midline, so its right face is 10 cm right of the midline: 550 mm along the counter from the toddler's end. All loose objects stand on the counter and are centred 29 cm in front of the arm bases unless stated. A kitchen knife in a grey plastic blade guard, modelled as a 150 x 30 x 25 mm box (100 g), lies flat with its long side pointing away from the arms, its centre 27 cm left of the midline. A red ceramic mug without a handle (70 mm across, 80 mm tall, 300 g) stands upright 21 cm in front of the arm bases, 15 cm left of the midline. An orange plastic pill bottle (40 mm across, 60 mm tall, 80 g) stands upright 36 cm in front of the arm bases, 17 cm left of the midline. A green plastic sippy cup (60 mm across, 100 mm tall, 150 g) stands upright 34 cm right of the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Distances are measured along the counter (side to side) from its left end, the toddler's end. An object 'at rest' is moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s. Each hazard (knife, mug, pill bottle) earns 0.2 when it is at rest on the counter top itself (its bottom within 5 mm of the top, not on the divider or another object), lies or stands as stated (the knife on any of its four long faces, its long side tilted at most 15 degrees from level; the mug and bottle upright, tilted at most 15 degrees; any turn about the vertical), and its nearest point is at least 550 mm from the toddler's end, i.e. it is wholly right of the divider. The sippy cup earns 0.4 when it is at rest upright on the counter top (tilted at most 15 degrees) with its centre at most 150 mm from the toddler's end, but only while every hazard's nearest point is at least 550 mm from that end, so the cup never counts while a hazard is still within the toddler's reach. All of it: 1.0. The score is 0 if any of the four loose objects is off the counter (its centre outside the board's outline, such as on the table, the stool or the floor, or its bottom 10 mm or more below the counter top). Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Put the knife, mug and pill bottle back at their marks on the counter's left half and the sippy cup at its mark on the far right; tape outlines on the counter make this quick. The counter, the divider and the stool marker are clamped or taped down and never move.
fidelity: Approximate: the knife is a rigid box (a knife in its blade guard), the mug a solid handleless cylinder with no liquid, and the bottle and sippy cup solid cylinders. The scorer reads only the final layout, so a mug tipped on the way and stood back up is not penalised. The toddler is not modelled; the stool marker and the 550 mm line stand in for its reach. All objects have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
